shouldFix.title: The operative definition of the amended set names a set D-010 never contributed to, states no cardinality, and admits a reading that moves three deferral-limb rows onto the SATISFIED limb
shouldFix.finding: Decision 1 reads: 'Add only DR-131 and DR-133 to D-002's condition-2 affected-row set. After this entry that set is the adopted D-002/D-010 set plus DR-131 and DR-133.' Measured at the bytes, there is no 'D-002/D-010 affected-row set'. D-002's condition-2 affected-row set is 21 rows: DR-101, 102, 103, 104, 105, 107, 111, 112, 114, 115, 117, 118, 119, 120, 121, 122, 123, 124, 125, 126, 127. D-010 contributed nothing to it — its Decision adds register row DR-130 with slice 1's deferral disposition recorded in the row itself, and file 08's own condition-2 note records that DR-128/129 entered the literal text 'benign because both carry D-002 dispositions'. All three D-010 rows are on the DEFERRAL limb, which this same entry preserves two clauses earlier under Stands. A reader who takes 'the adopted D-002/D-010 set' as the union of rows those two decisions name gets 24, and the amended affected set becomes 26 — silently moving DR-128, DR-129 and DR-130 off the deferral limb and onto the limb that requires SATISFIED. That contradicts D-002's deferrals, D-010's own disposition, file 08's condition-2 note, and the adopted D-133's partition, all in the entry whose sole subject is this set. The entry also never states the resulting cardinality, so no authority-bearing document says how large the amended set is: file 12 carries '4/30 → 4/32' but is marked 'DRAFT GOAL — no authority'.
shouldFix.whyNotMustFix: The harmful reading is contradicted elsewhere in the same entry — Decision 1's first sentence says 'D-002's condition-2 affected-row set', and the Stands list preserves the deferrals verbatim — so nothing is actually decided wrongly. This is an ambiguity in the operative sentence of a set-amendment decision, not a wrong amendment.
shouldFix.repair: State the set by measurement rather than by a compound reference. For example: 'D-002's condition-2 affected-row set is the 21 rows DR-101, 102, 103, 104, 105, 107, 111, 112, 114, 115, 117, 118, 119, 120, 121, 122, 123, 124, 125, 126, 127. After this entry it is those 21 plus DR-131 and DR-133 = 23. The deferral limb is unchanged at 9 rows (DR-106, 108, 109, 110, 113, 116, 128, 129, 130). Once the later MF-6 act creates the two cells the register carries 32 rows, each on exactly one limb.' That removes the ambiguity, supplies the cardinality the later MF-6 act needs from an authority-bearing source, and matches the corpus's own practice of recording set arithmetic (D-002's turn-3 verdict re-verified 27/27 + 22/22; adopted D-133 carries a 4 + 5 + 12 + 9 = 30 partition).

shouldFix.title: The requiring authority is quoted as a single D-018 passage but is assembled from two, and the authority that precisely authorizes the act is not cited
shouldFix.finding: The Why-clause opens: 'D-018 §2: changing D-002's command set, language-role set, platform set, deferral set, identity-dependency rides, condition-2 affected-row set, or condition-4 required-gate set is a scoped D-002 successor with its own D-000 review.' No passage of D-018 says that. D-018's Decision item 2 supplies the successor requirement — 'This entry does not add or remove commands, language roles, platforms, deferrals, identity rides, or gates from D-002 … If chosen later, that is a scoped D-002 successor with its own D-000 review' — but its list is SIX items and does not include the condition-2 affected-row set. The seven-item list that does include it sits in D-018's Decision-type bullet, which states only what D-018 itself does not change and imposes no successor requirement. The entry fuses the seven-item list from one passage with the requirement sentence from another and labels the result 'D-018 §2'. A later reader who checks D-018 §2 will not find it. Separately, the authority that authorizes this exact act in terms — D-132 clause 3, 'after D-000 review, a scoped D-002 successor that adds only DR-131 and DR-133 to the condition-2 affected-row set' — appears nowhere in the Why-clause, though D-132's commit is pinned in the measured inputs. The entry leads with an inaccurate citation and omits the accurate one. I record that I propagated this same misreading in the first consensus round, and file 12 §6.3 repeats it; the measurement corrects all three.
shouldFix.whyNotMustFix: The conclusion is right and the act is properly authorized: D-132 clause 3 authorizes it in terms, D-001 SF-3 independently makes growing condition 2's quantifier a recorded reviewed decision, and D-018's Decision-type bullet plus item 2 read together plainly extend the principle. Nothing is unlawful; the citation is.
shouldFix.repair: Split the citation to match the bytes and lead with the act's actual authority. For example: 'D-132 clause 3 authorizes a scoped D-002 successor adding only DR-131 and DR-133 to the condition-2 affected-row set. D-001 SF-3 makes growing condition 2's quantifier a recorded reviewed decision. D-018's Decision-type bullet names the condition-2 affected-row set among the D-002 sets it does not change, and its Decision item 2 requires a scoped D-002 successor with its own D-000 review for the six sets it enumerates; the same requirement governs the affected-row set by that entry's own scope statement.' That is accurate at every clause and strictly stronger than the fused version.

advisories.finding: Between this entry and the later MF-6 act, D-002's amended set names two rows the register does not contain — the mirror image of the file-08-versus-D-002 disagreement this successor exists to prevent. Decision 3 discloses most of it ('named future rows, not live file-08 cells', 'Condition 2's live count stays 4 of 30') but does not say what happens if readiness is evaluated inside the window.
advisories.whyNotBlocking: The window is benign in this direction and is D-132's own sequencing (clause 3 before clause 4). D-001 SF-3 already settles it: condition 2's quantifier is evaluated over the register as it stands, so two names with no referent neither add to nor subtract from the count, and condition 2 is NOT MET regardless.
advisories.suggestion: Add one clause to Decision 3: if readiness is evaluated before the MF-6 act lands, condition 2 quantifies over the register as it stands (D-001 SF-3) and the two named rows have no referent, so the evaluation is unaffected.

advisories.finding: The entry carries no honesty-about-the-trade paragraph. D-000 clause 5 discipline is visible in D-002, D-018 and D-056, each of which states what its decision gives up. D-134's own readiness effect is genuinely zero, but the act it sets up will add two OPEN rows, taking condition 2 from 4 of 30 to 4 of 32 — further from MET, in service of making the architecture answerable rather than closable by omission.
advisories.whyNotBlocking: D-134's stated readiness effect is accurate as written, and the disclosure properly belongs to the MF-6 act that moves the denominator. Nothing here overclaims.
advisories.suggestion: One sentence recording the trade — two more OPEN rows now, a lawful and answerable condition 2 later — so the entry that authorizes the growth is also the entry that names its cost.

coordinatorSummary: OBJECT at 0 MUST-FIX and 2 SHOULD-FIX, with 2 non-blocking advisories. Twenty attacks run, four landed. Custody is intact: subject 722bf2ea at 0444 unmoved, HEAD never left 5b6f723, file 08 at 1cdcf9d4 unmodified across C-D133 — direct proof that D-133 kept its no-file-08-edit promise — and COORD's growth since D-132 is append-only, the D-133 entry alone. All five measured-inputs rows reproduce, and the adopted D-133 matches the turn-3 subject I consented to, so D-134's reliance on it is sound. The act itself is right and properly authorized by D-132 clause 3, and every recital of D-002's surface — commands, TypeScript-only role, the four platforms, the nine-row deferral list, identity rides, the condition-4 gate set — reproduces from D-002's bytes unaltered. Two sentences do not survive measurement. First, Decision 1 defines the amended set as 'the adopted D-002/D-010 set plus DR-131 and DR-133', but there is no such joint set: D-002's affected-row set is 21 rows, and D-010 contributed only DR-130 — plus DR-128/129 entering the literal text — all three to the DEFERRAL limb, as this same entry's Stands list preserves. Read as a union, the amendment would sweep DR-128, DR-129 and DR-130 onto the limb that requires SATISFIED, contradicting D-002, D-010, file 08's own condition-2 note and adopted D-133's partition. The entry also states no cardinality, so no authority-bearing document says the amended set is 23 — file 12 carries the numbers but is expressly authority-free. Second, the Why-clause quotes 'D-018 §2' for a sentence D-018 does not contain: item 2 supplies the successor requirement over six sets and does not name the condition-2 affected-row set, while the seven-item list that names it sits in the Decision-type bullet and imposes no requirement. The two are fused and mislabelled, and D-132 clause 3 — which authorizes this act in terms — is absent from the Why-clause entirely. I record that I propagated that same misreading in the first consensus round and that file 12 §6.3 repeats it; the measurement corrects my text too. Both repairs are one sentence each and everything else in the entry should carry into turn 2 unchanged.
